model_annotation: The image displays two line plots, labeled A and B, both illustrating trends over time from 2008 to 2021. Plot A shows the average growing season length in days, with the y-axis ranging from 200 to 280 days and the x-axis representing years. The red line, marked with circular data points, begins at approximately 280 days in 2008, dips to about 265 days around 2012–2013, continues to decline to roughly 240 days in 2017, and then falls further to approximately 200 days by 2021. Plot B depicts the structural effect above average growing season length as a percentage, with the y-axis ranging from 0.0 to 2.0 percent and the x-axis also representing years. The red line, also marked with circular data points, starts at about 1.5% in 2008, decreases to a minimum of approximately 0.8% around 2012–2013, rises to about 1.3% in 2017, and then sharply increases to nearly 2.0% by 2021. Both plots use a linear scale on the x-axis and a linear scale on the y-axis, with tick marks approximately every 4 years on the x-axis and every 0.5 unit on the y-axis for Plot B.
